column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)

bio|02-06|1912|Εύα Μπράουν|Eva Braun|Eva Braun was born in Munich and was the companion of Adolf Hitler for many years. She married Hitler in the Berlin bunker at the end of April 1945, a few hours before the two of them took their own lives.

bio|02-06|1918|Γκούσταφ Κλιμτ|Gustav Klimt|Gustav Klimt was an Austrian painter and a leading figure of Austrian symbolism and of the Secession in Vienna. He became known for works such as "The Kiss" and the portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer, which use gold leaf.

bio|02-06|1932|Φρανσουά Τρυφώ|Francois Truffaut|Francois Truffaut was a French film director and critic and one of the pioneers of the French "New Wave". He directed "The 400 Blows", "Jules and Jim" and "Day for Night".

bio|02-06|1945|Μπομπ Μάρλεϊ|Bob Marley|Bob Marley was born in Jamaica and became the most famous reggae musician. With the Wailers he sang hits such as "No Woman, No Cry" and "One Love", with messages of peace and social justice. He died of cancer in 1981.

bio|02-06|1952|Γεώργιος ΣΤ΄|George VI|George VI was king of the United Kingdom from 1936, when his brother Edward VIII abdicated, until 1952. He led the country in the Second World War and was the father of Elizabeth II. He died in 1952.

bio|02-07|1478|Τόμας Μορ|Thomas More|Thomas More was an English lawyer, politician and writer. He wrote the work "Utopia" and was Lord Chancellor to Henry VIII. He refused to recognise the king as head of the Church and was beheaded in 1535. The Catholic Church declared him a saint.

bio|02-07|1812|Τσαρλς Ντίκενς|Charles Dickens|Charles Dickens was an English writer of the Victorian era. He wrote novels such as "Oliver Twist", "Great Expectations" and "A Christmas Carol", with sharp social criticism and unforgettable characters.

bio|02-07|1864|Βουκ Στεφάνοβιτς Κάρατζιτς|Vuk Karadzic|Vuk Karadzic was a Serbian philologist. He reformed the Serbian alphabet and spelling on the basis of pronunciation, and he collected folk songs and folk tales. He is one of the founders of the modern Serbian language.

bio|02-07|1870|Άλφρεντ Άντλερ|Alfred Adler|Alfred Adler was an Austrian doctor and psychologist. He was at first a collaborator of Freud and founded the school of individual psychology. He introduced the concept of the "inferiority complex".

bio|02-07|1877|Γκόντφρεϊ Χάρολντ Χάρντι|Godfrey Harold Hardy|Godfrey Harold Hardy was an English mathematician. He worked on number theory and mathematical analysis, collaborated with Littlewood and discovered the talent of the Indian mathematician Ramanujan. He wrote "A Mathematician's Apology".

bio|02-07|1885|Σίνκλερ Λιούις|Sinclair Lewis|Sinclair Lewis was an American writer. He wrote novels with social satire, such as "Main Street" and "Babbitt". In 1930 he became the first American to be honoured with the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|02-07|1894|Αντόλφ Σαξ|Adolphe Sax|Adolphe Sax was a Belgian maker of musical instruments. Around 1840 he invented the saxophone and also made other instruments, such as the saxhorn. He settled in Paris and made his business famous.

bio|02-07|1979|Γιόζεφ Μένγκελε|Josef Mengele|Josef Mengele was a German SS doctor at the Auschwitz camp. He carried out inhumane experiments on prisoners, mainly on twins. After the war he fled to South America and was never tried. He died in Brazil in 1979.

bio|02-07|2020|Λι Ουενλιάνγκ|Li Wenliang|Li Wenliang was a Chinese ophthalmologist in Wuhan. At the end of 2019 he warned colleagues about a new illness that resembled SARS, and he was punished by the local authorities. He died of Covid-19 in February 2020.

bio|02-08|1587|Μαρία Α΄|Mary, Queen of Scots|Mary Stuart was queen of Scotland. She became queen as an infant and ruled from 1561. She was forced to abdicate and took refuge in England, where Elizabeth I imprisoned her and then condemned her for conspiracy. She was executed in 1587.

bio|02-08|1700|Ντάνιελ Μπερνούλι|Daniel Bernoulli|Daniel Bernoulli was a Swiss mathematician and physicist. In his work "Hydrodynamica" he formulated Bernoulli's principle on the speed and pressure of fluids, and he also did work on probability theory.

bio|02-08|1725|Πέτρος Α΄|Peter the Great|Peter the Great was tsar of Russia from 1682 and emperor from 1721. He modernised the country, created a navy, built Saint Petersburg and defeated the Swedes in the Great Northern War. He died in 1725.

bio|02-08|1819|Τζον Ράσκιν|John Ruskin|John Ruskin was an English art critic and thinker. He wrote "Modern Painters" and "The Stones of Venice" and defended Gothic architecture. He also dealt with questions of social justice.

bio|02-08|1828|Ιούλιος Βερν|Jules Verne|Jules Verne was a French writer and a pioneer of science fiction. He wrote "Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea", "Journey to the Center of the Earth" and "Around the World in Eighty Days".

bio|02-08|1834|Ντμίτρι Μεντελέγιεφ|Dmitri Mendeleev|Dmitri Mendeleev was a Russian chemist. In 1869 he created the periodic table of the elements, in which he arranged them according to atomic weight and their properties, and he predicted elements that were discovered later.

bio|02-08|1921|Πιοτρ Κροπότκιν|Peter Kropotkin|Peter Kropotkin was a Russian anarchist thinker and geographer. He wrote "Mutual Aid", where he argued that cooperation is a factor of evolution, and "The Conquest of Bread". He lived in exile for many years.

bio|02-08|1931|Τζέιμς Ντιν|James Dean|James Dean was an American actor. He became a symbol of teenage rebellion with the film "Rebel Without a Cause". He appeared in "East of Eden" and "Giant". He died in a car accident in 1955, at the age of 24.

bio|02-08|1957|Τζον φον Νόιμαν|John von Neumann|John von Neumann was born in Budapest. He was a mathematician and physicist and contributed to game theory, quantum mechanics and the architecture of electronic computers. He lived in the United States and died in 1957.

bio|02-09|1737|Τόμας Πέιν|Thomas Paine|Thomas Paine was born in England and lived in the United States. He wrote the pamphlet "Common Sense", which encouraged American independence, and "The Rights of Man", in support of the French Revolution.

bio|02-09|1773|Ουίλιαμ Χένρι Χάρισον|William Henry Harrison|William Henry Harrison was the 9th president of the United States. He was a general and governor and won the elections of 1840. He died only a month after his inauguration in 1841, with the shortest presidency in the history of the United States.

bio|02-09|1881|Φιοντόρ Ντοστογιέφσκι|Fyodor Dostoevsky|Fyodor Dostoevsky was a Russian writer. He wrote the novels "Crime and Punishment", "The Idiot" and "The Brothers Karamazov", which examine deep psychological and philosophical questions. He died in Saint Petersburg.

bio|02-09|1940|Τζον Μάξγουελ Κούτσι|J. M. Coetzee|J. M. Coetzee is a South African writer, known for the novels "Waiting for the Barbarians" and "Disgrace". In 2003 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|02-09|1943|Τζόζεφ Στίγκλιτς|Joseph Stiglitz|Joseph Stiglitz is an American economist. He studied markets and information, and in 2001 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics. He is also known for his views on globalisation and inequality.

bio|02-09|1944|Άλις Γουόκερ|Alice Walker|Alice Walker is an American writer and activist. She wrote the novel "The Color Purple", for which she received the Pulitzer Prize in 1983. She has also written poetry and essays on women's rights.
bio|02-09|1979|Ντένις Γκέιμπορ|Dennis Gabor|Dennis Gabor was born in Budapest and lived in Britain. He was a physicist and invented holography. In 1971 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|02-09|1984|Γιούρι Αντρόπωφ|Yuri Andropov|Yuri Andropov was a Soviet politician. He led the KGB for many years and succeeded Brezhnev as general secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union in 1982. He died after fifteen months in power, and he was succeeded by Chernenko.

bio|02-09|2001|Χέρμπερτ Σάιμον|Herbert Simon|Herbert Simon was an American economist and computer scientist. He studied decision-making in organisations and artificial intelligence. In 1978 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics.

bio|02-10|1755|Μοντεσκιέ|Montesquieu|Charles de Montesquieu died in Paris in 1755. He was a French philosopher of the Enlightenment. He wrote "The Spirit of the Laws", in which he argues for the separation of powers, and the "Persian Letters".

bio|02-10|1837|Αλεξάντρ Σεργκέγεβιτς Πούσκιν|Alexander Pushkin|Alexander Pushkin was a Russian poet and writer and is regarded as the founder of modern Russian literature. He wrote "Eugene Onegin" and "Boris Godunov". He was killed in a duel in 1837.

bio|02-10|1890|Μπορίς Παστερνάκ|Boris Pasternak|Boris Pasternak was a Russian poet and writer. He wrote the novel "Doctor Zhivago", which was banned in the Soviet Union. In 1958 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature, but he was forced to refuse it.

bio|02-10|1894|Χάρολντ Μακμίλαν|Harold Macmillan|Harold Macmillan was a British Conservative politician. He was prime minister from 1957 to 1963 and in his "Wind of Change" speech supported the decolonisation of Africa. He resigned after the Profumo affair.

bio|02-10|1898|Μπέρτολτ Μπρεχτ|Bertolt Brecht|Bertolt Brecht was a German playwright and poet. He created "epic theatre" and wrote plays such as "The Threepenny Opera" and "Mother Courage and Her Children". He was forced to leave Nazi Germany and returned in 1949.

bio|02-10|1902|Γουόλτερ Χάουζερ Μπράταιην|Walter Houser Brattain|Walter Houser Brattain was an American physicist. At Bell Laboratories he contributed to the development of the transistor. In 1956 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physics with John Bardeen and William Shockley.

bio|02-10|1923|Βίλχελμ Κόνραντ Ρέντγκεν|Wilhelm Conrad Rontgen|Wilhelm Rontgen was a German physicist. In 1895 he discovered X-rays and in 1901 he became the first person to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He did not patent the discovery, so that it would be free for everyone.
bio|02-10|1952|Λι Σιεν Λουνγκ|Lee Hsien Loong|Lee Hsien Loong is a Singaporean politician, the son of the country's founder Lee Kuan Yew. He was prime minister of Singapore from 2004 to 2024.

bio|02-10|2005|Άρθουρ Μίλερ|Arthur Miller|Arthur Miller was an American playwright. He wrote "Death of a Salesman" and "The Crucible", a play about McCarthyism. He was married to Marilyn Monroe. He died in 2005.

bio|02-11|1650|Ρενέ Ντεκάρτ|Rene Descartes|Rene Descartes was a French philosopher and mathematician. He wrote the "Discourse on the Method", in which he formulated "I think, therefore I am". He introduced Cartesian coordinates. He died in Stockholm.

bio|02-11|1847|Τόμας Έντισον|Thomas Edison|Thomas Edison was an American inventor and businessman. He improved the electric light bulb, invented the phonograph and founded the first industrial research laboratory. He holds more than a thousand patents.

bio|02-11|1900|Χανς-Γκέοργκ Γκάνταμερ|Hans-Georg Gadamer|Hans-Georg Gadamer was a German philosopher. His main work, "Truth and Method", developed hermeneutic philosophy. He lived for more than 100 years and died in 2002.

bio|02-11|1947|Γιούκιο Χατογιάμα|Yukio Hatoyama|Yukio Hatoyama is a Japanese politician and was prime minister of Japan in 2009-2010. He led the Democratic Party, which ended the long rule of the Liberal Democratic Party.

bio|02-11|1948|Σεργκέι Αϊζενστάιν|Sergei Eisenstein|Sergei Eisenstein died in Moscow in 1948. He was a Soviet film director and theorist of cinema, creator of "Battleship Potemkin" and "Ivan the Terrible", and a pioneer of the art of montage.

bio|02-11|1963|Σύλβια Πλαθ|Sylvia Plath|Sylvia Plath was an American poet and writer. She wrote the collection "Ariel" and the novel "The Bell Jar". Her poetry is confessional. She took her own life in London in 1963, at the age of thirty.

bio|02-11|1969|Τζένιφερ Άνιστον|Jennifer Aniston|Jennifer Aniston is an American actress. She became known throughout the world for the role of Rachel in the series "Friends", and she appeared in films such as "Marley & Me" and "The Break-Up".

bio|02-11|1992|Τέιλορ Λότνερ|Taylor Lautner|Taylor Lautner is an American actor. He became known for the role of Jacob in the "Twilight" film series. He has also appeared in other action and drama films.

bio|02-11|2012|Γουίτνεϋ Χιούστον|Whitney Houston|Whitney Houston was an American singer and actress. She was one of the most successful singers of the 1980s and 1990s, with songs such as "I Will Always Love You". She died in 2012 in Los Angeles.

bio|02-12|712|Του Φου|Du Fu|Du Fu was a Chinese poet of the Tang dynasty. He was born in 712 and wrote poems with historical and social content. He is regarded as one of the greatest poets of Chinese literature, together with Li Bai.
bio|02-12|1768|Φραγκίσκος Β΄|Francis II|Francis II was the last emperor of the Holy Roman Empire. In 1806, after Napoleon's victories, he dissolved the empire and continued as Francis I of Austria.

bio|02-12|1804|Ιμμάνουελ Καντ|Immanuel Kant|Immanuel Kant was a German philosopher from Konigsberg. He wrote the "Critique of Pure Reason", the "Critique of Practical Reason" and the "Critique of Judgement". He is regarded as one of the greatest philosophers of the West.

bio|02-12|1809|Κάρολος Δαρβίνος|Charles Darwin|Charles Darwin was an English naturalist. He sailed on the ship Beagle and observed nature. In his work "On the Origin of Species" of 1859 he presented the theory of evolution through natural selection.

bio|02-12|1809|Αβραάμ Λίνκολν|Abraham Lincoln|Abraham Lincoln was the 16th president of the United States. He led the country through the American Civil War, signed the Emancipation Proclamation and supported the abolition of slavery. He was assassinated in 1865.

bio|02-12|1881|Άννα Πάβλοβα|Anna Pavlova|Anna Pavlova was a Russian ballerina and one of the greatest of classical ballet. She became famous with the performance of "The Dying Swan". She toured the whole world and made ballet known to new audiences.

bio|02-12|1884|Μαξ Μπέκμαν|Max Beckmann|Max Beckmann was a German expressionist painter. His paintings and triptychs with symbolic themes express the turbulent era in which he lived. The Nazis labelled him a "degenerate artist", and he lived in exile in the United States.

bio|02-12|1949|Χασάν αλ-Μπάννα|Hassan al-Banna|Hassan al-Banna was an Egyptian teacher. In 1928 he founded the Muslim Brotherhood, an organisation that combines religious activity with social work. He was assassinated in Cairo in 1949.

bio|02-12|1954|Τζίγκα Βερτόφ|Dziga Vertov|Dziga Vertov was a Soviet film director and theorist of the documentary. His film "Man with a Movie Camera" of 1929 is a landmark of experimental cinema. He believed in "kino-truth".

bio|02-12|1979|Ζαν Ρενουάρ|Jean Renoir|Jean Renoir was a French film director and the son of the painter Auguste Renoir. He directed "The Grand Illusion" and "The Rules of the Game", films regarded as among the most important in French cinema.

bio|02-13|1258|Οσμάν Α΄|Osman I|Osman I was the founder of the Ottoman Empire, whose dynasty took its name from him. He led a small Turkish emirate in Bithynia, on the border with Byzantium, and expanded it around 1300.

bio|02-13|1542|Αικατερίνη Χάουαρντ|Catherine Howard|Catherine Howard was the fifth wife of King Henry VIII of England. She married him in 1540 and was accused of adultery. She was beheaded on 13 February 1542, at the age of around twenty.

bio|02-13|1571|Μπενβενούτο Τσελίνι|Benvenuto Cellini|Benvenuto Cellini was an Italian Renaissance sculptor and goldsmith. He created the salt cellar "Saliera" and the statue of Perseus. He also left an autobiography with a vivid description of his era.

bio|02-13|1660|Κάρολος Ι΄ Γουσταύος|Charles X Gustav|Charles X Gustav was king of Sweden from 1654 to 1660. He waged wars with Poland and Denmark and gained territories through the Treaty of Roskilde. He died in 1660.

bio|02-13|1766|Τόμας Μάλθους|Thomas Malthus|Thomas Malthus was an English economist and demographer. In his "Essay on the Principle of Population" he argued that population grows faster than food, which would cause famines. His arguments influenced Darwin.

bio|02-13|1883|Ρίχαρντ Βάγκνερ|Richard Wagner|Richard Wagner was a German composer. He wrote operas such as "Tristan und Isolde" and the cycle "The Ring of the Nibelung". He founded the Bayreuth Festival. He died in Venice in 1883.

bio|02-13|1910|Γουίλλιαμ Μπράντφορντ Σόκλεϋ|William Bradford Shockley|William Shockley was an American physicist. Together with Bardeen and Brattain he invented the transistor, for which they shared the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1956. Later he caused controversy with his views on heredity.

bio|02-13|1974|Ρόμπι Γουίλιαμς|Robbie Williams|Robbie Williams is an English singer. He began as a member of Take That and continued as a solo artist with hits such as "Angels" and "Let Me Entertain You". He has won many Brit Awards.

bio|02-13|1979|Άντερς Μπέρινγκ Μπρέιβικ|Anders Behring Breivik|Anders Behring Breivik is a Norwegian far-right extremist. On 22 July 2011 he killed eight people with a bomb in Oslo and 69 people by shooting on the island of Utoya. He was sentenced to 21 years in prison, with the possibility of extension.

bio|02-14|1400|Ριχάρδος Β΄|Richard II|Richard II was king of England from 1377, when he became king at the age of ten. He faced the Peasants' Revolt of 1381 and rebellious nobles. He was deposed in 1399 by his cousin Henry and died in prison.
bio|02-14|1483|Μπαμπούρ|Babur|Babur was a descendant of Timur and Genghis Khan. He was the founder of the Mughal Empire in India and captured Delhi in 1526. He also wrote memoirs, the "Baburnama".

bio|02-14|1779|Τζέιμς Κουκ|James Cook|James Cook was a British sailor and explorer. He made three voyages in the Pacific, mapped New Zealand and the east coast of Australia, and became the first European to reach Hawaii. He was killed there in 1779.

bio|02-14|1818|Φρέντερικ Ντάγκλας|Frederick Douglass|Frederick Douglass was born a slave in Maryland and escaped. He became a leader of the movement against slavery, an outstanding orator and writer. He wrote an autobiography and became an adviser to President Lincoln.

bio|02-14|1869|Τσαρλς Τόμσον Ρις Γουίλσον|Charles Thomson Rees Wilson|Charles Wilson was a Scottish physicist. He invented the cloud chamber (the Wilson chamber), which makes it possible to observe the tracks of charged particles. In 1927 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|02-14|1943|Ντάβιντ Χίλμπερτ|David Hilbert|David Hilbert died in Gottingen in 1943. He was a German mathematician who contributed to geometry, algebra and the foundations of mathematics, and in 1900 he formulated 23 unsolved problems.

bio|02-14|1967|Μαρκ Ρούτε|Mark Rutte|Mark Rutte is a Dutch politician. He was prime minister of the Netherlands from 2010 to 2024 and leader of the VVD party. In 2024 he became secretary general of NATO.

bio|02-14|1970|Σάιμον Πεγκ|Simon Pegg|Simon Pegg is an English actor and screenwriter. He became known for the comedy "Shaun of the Dead" and played Scotty in the "Star Trek" films. He also appears in the "Mission: Impossible" film series.

bio|02-14|2005|Ραφίκ Χαρίρι|Rafik Hariri|Rafik Hariri was a Lebanese businessman and politician. He was prime minister of Lebanon and helped rebuild the country after the civil war. He was assassinated by a car bomb in Beirut in 2005.

bio|02-15|1564|Γαλιλαίος Γαλιλέι|Galileo Galilei|Galileo Galilei was born in Pisa. He was an astronomer and physicist and used the telescope to observe the moons of Jupiter. He supported the heliocentric system, for which he was condemned by the Church.

bio|02-15|1710|Λουδοβίκος ΙΕ΄|Louis XV|Louis XV was king of France from 1715 to 1774. He became king as a child and his reign was long. France lost colonies in the Seven Years' War, and the finances of the state deteriorated.

bio|02-15|1748|Τζέρεμι Μπένθαμ|Jeremy Bentham|Jeremy Bentham was an English philosopher and lawyer. He founded the philosophy of utilitarianism, which holds that actions should be judged by the greatest happiness of the greatest number.

bio|02-15|1781|Γκότχολντ Εφραίμ Λέσσινγκ|Gotthold Ephraim Lessing|Gotthold Ephraim Lessing was a German writer and critic of the Enlightenment. He wrote the play "Nathan the Wise", a work on tolerance, and theoretical essays such as "Laocoon".

bio|02-15|1861|Σαρλ Εντουάρ Γκιγιόμ|Charles Edouard Guillaume|Charles Edouard Guillaume was a Swiss physicist. He discovered the alloys Invar and Elinvar, which hardly expand with temperature. In 1920 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|02-15|1874|Έρνεστ Σάκλετον|Ernest Shackleton|Ernest Shackleton was born in Ireland and was an Antarctic explorer. The "Endurance" expedition of 1914 lost its ship in the ice, and he led all his men to rescue, with no losses.

bio|02-15|1959|Όουεν Γουίλανς Ρίτσαρντσον|Owen Willans Richardson|Owen Richardson was an English physicist. He studied the thermionic emission of electrons from hot metals. In 1928 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|02-15|1965|Νατ Κινγκ Κόουλ|Nat King Cole|Nat King Cole was an American jazz singer and pianist. His smooth voice made hits of the songs "Unforgettable" and "Mona Lisa". He died of lung cancer in 1965.

bio|02-15|1988|Ρίτσαρντ Φίλλιπς Φάινμαν|Richard Feynman|Richard Feynman was an American physicist. He contributed to quantum electrodynamics, for which he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1965. He was also known for his lectures and the book "Feynman Lectures on Physics".

bio|02-16|1497|Φίλιππος Μελάγχθων|Philipp Melanchthon|Philipp Melanchthon was a German theologian and philologist. He worked with Luther in the Reformation and wrote the "Augsburg Confession", a basic confession of the Lutherans. His surname is the Greek translation of his German family name, Schwarzerd.

bio|02-16|1822|Φράνσις Γκάλτον|Francis Galton|Francis Galton was an English scientist. He was a cousin of Darwin and a pioneer of statistics and psychometrics. He introduced the term "eugenics" and the use of fingerprints for identification.

bio|02-16|1834|Ερνστ Χέκελ|Ernst Haeckel|Ernst Haeckel was a German zoologist and philosopher. He supported Darwin's ideas in Germany and introduced terms such as "ecology". He created famous illustrations of marine organisms.

bio|02-16|1848|Οκτάβ Μιρμπώ|Octave Mirbeau|Octave Mirbeau was a French writer and journalist. He wrote the novel "The Diary of a Chambermaid" and the play "Business Is Business". He was a champion of Dreyfus.

bio|02-16|1907|Τζοζουέ Καρντούτσι|Giosue Carducci|Giosue Carducci was an Italian poet and scholar. In 1906 he became the first Italian to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He was a professor at Bologna.
bio|02-16|1917|Οκτάβ Μιρμπώ|Octave Mirbeau|Octave Mirbeau died in Paris in 1917. He was a French writer with sharp social criticism. He wrote "The Diary of a Chambermaid" and works for the theatre.

bio|02-16|1941|Κιμ Γιονγκ Ιλ|Kim Jong Il|Kim Jong Il was the leader of North Korea from 1994 to 2011, when his father Kim Il Sung died. He headed an authoritarian regime and developed the country's nuclear weapons programme.

bio|02-16|2016|Μπούτρος Μπούτρος - Γκάλι|Boutros Boutros-Ghali|Boutros Boutros-Ghali was an Egyptian diplomat and politician. He was the sixth secretary-general of the United Nations, from 1992 to 1996. He died in 2016.

bio|02-16|2024|Αλεξέι Ναβάλνι|Alexei Navalny|Alexei Navalny was a Russian lawyer and opposition politician. He denounced corruption in the government of Putin and greatly increased his popularity. He was arrested in 2021 and died in prison in February 2024.

bio|02-17|1600|Τζορντάνο Μπρούνο|Giordano Bruno|Giordano Bruno was an Italian philosopher and Dominican friar. He argued that the universe is infinite and that the stars are other suns. The Inquisition condemned him, and he was burned in Rome in 1600.
bio|02-17|1673|Μολιέρος|Moliere|Moliere died in 1673 just after a performance of his play "The Imaginary Invalid", in which he played the leading role. He was the greatest comic playwright of France.

bio|02-17|1856|Χάινριχ Χάινε|Heinrich Heine|Heinrich Heine was a German poet and journalist of Jewish descent. He wrote the "Book of Songs", which was set to music by many composers. He lived in Paris in his last years and died there.

bio|02-17|1888|Όττο Στερν|Otto Stern|Otto Stern was a German physicist. Together with Walther Gerlach he carried out the Stern-Gerlach experiment, which showed the quantisation of angular momentum. In 1943 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|02-17|1963|Μάικλ Τζόρνταν|Michael Jordan|Michael Jordan is a former American basketball player. He won six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls and is considered the best player of all time. He also won two Olympic gold medals.

bio|02-17|1972|Μπίλι Τζο Άρμστρονγκ|Billie Joe Armstrong|Billie Joe Armstrong is an American musician, singer and guitarist of Green Day. The band became very well known with albums such as "Dookie" and "American Idiot".

bio|02-17|1981|Πάρις Χίλτον|Paris Hilton|Paris Hilton is an American businesswoman and socialite, heiress of the Hilton hotel family. She became known through the television series "The Simple Life" and through her businesses in perfumes and fashion.

bio|02-17|1981|Τζόζεφ Γκόρντον-Λέβιτ|Joseph Gordon-Levitt|Joseph Gordon-Levitt is an American actor. He became known for the films "500 Days of Summer", "Inception" and "The Dark Knight Rises". He has also directed films.

bio|02-17|1986|Τζίντου Κρισναμούρτι|Jiddu Krishnamurti|Jiddu Krishnamurti was an Indian thinker and speaker. He taught that truth is not reached through organisations or teachers but through personal observation. He dissolved the Order of the Star, which had been founded for him.

bio|02-18|1405|Ταμερλάνος|Timur|Timur was a leader and conqueror from Central Asia. He built a great empire with its capital at Samarkand. He defeated the Ottoman sultan Bayezid at Ankara in 1402. He died on the way to China.

bio|02-18|1516|Μαρία Α΄|Mary I|Mary I was queen of England from 1553 to 1558. She was the daughter of Henry VIII and tried to restore Catholicism, with many Protestants executed, which is why she is remembered as "Bloody Mary".

bio|02-18|1546|Μαρτίνος Λούθηρος|Martin Luther|Martin Luther was a German theologian and monk. In 1517 he wrote the "95 Theses" against indulgences and started the Reformation. He translated the Bible into German. He died in 1546.

bio|02-18|1564|Μιχαήλ Άγγελος|Michelangelo|Michelangelo was an Italian Renaissance sculptor, painter and architect. He created "David" and the "Pieta", painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel and designed the dome of Saint Peter's. He died in Rome.

bio|02-18|1745|Αλεσάντρο Βόλτα|Alessandro Volta|Alessandro Volta was an Italian physicist. In 1800 he invented the voltaic pile, the first electric battery. The unit of electric potential, the volt, is named after him.
